gen_risks.description: CRM system may not be ready by the November 2025 MVP, delaying school onboarding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set a detailed development plan, allocate dedicated team, conduct early user testing, and prepare a manual onboarding fallback.
gen_risks.evidence: We will develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Call-centre pilot could face implementation problems, affecting data collection support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pilot with limited scope, define clear SOPs, and retain alternative data-submission methods such as spreadsheet upload.
gen_risks.evidence: We will also start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection.

gen_risks.description: Food provided may not meet school food standards, leading to regulatory breach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Issue clear guidance, provide compliance checklists, and conduct periodic audits and training for schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Delay in HM Treasury approval could postpone funding and rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage Treasury early, submit detailed business case, secure provisional approval, and keep contingency cash reserves.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury.

gen_risks.description: Uncertainty over funding for future years may threaten programme sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a multi-year funding roadmap, demonstrate early benefits, and align with Treasury priorities.
gen_risks.evidence: Funding for future years will be agreed separately through business cases.

gen_risks.description: Cohort 1 may not start delivery in April 2026 as planned.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a detailed rollout checklist, monitor readiness weekly, and allocate contingency resources to meet the April 2026 target.
gen_risks.evidence: Cohort 1 will begin delivery in April 2026.

gen_risks.description: Transition from NSBP may be mistimed, creating a provision gap.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align transition timelines, provide bridge funding for July‑September 2026, and communicate clearly with affected schools.
gen_risks.evidence: All schools ... would be guaranteed a place ... after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient school applications could limit rollout reach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run targeted outreach, simplify the application process, and offer incentives such as priority support.
gen_risks.evidence: Schools with 40% or more FSM ... will be eligible to apply for a place.

gen_risks.description: Local authorities may lack capacity to support schools effectively.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide training, dedicated support staff, and monitor workload through regular reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: We will fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs.

gen_risks.description: Poor collaboration with sector partners could hinder delivery of advisory support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal partnership agreements, hold regular coordination meetings, and share performance metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on ... effective collaboration with the sector partners ...

gen_risks.description: Delay in the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill would postpone the statutory duty.
gen_risks.mitigation: Track legislative progress, engage MPs, and prepare interim guidance for schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools to offer a breakfast club.

gen_risks.description: Limited availability of skilled staff in DfE and the education sector may affect programme delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit temporary staff, cross‑train existing personnel, and offer retention incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Multi-layered governance could create decision‑making bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Streamline decision pathways, define clear escalation routes, and set decision‑making time‑boxes.
gen_risks.evidence: Programme governance is multi-layered, with primary oversight at the senior responsible officer (SRO) led 'free breakfast clubs project board'.

gen_risks.description: Area cost adjustments may cause funding mismatches due to labour‑market variations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Review area adjustments annually and adjust grant rates accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: Across all settings, we apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
